Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. As discussed, PulseAI is preparing to publish a bundled co-sell listing (US + EU regional availability) and we'd like to request a one-time listing credit to make the initial go-to-market economics work for our pilot customers.

High-level:
- Proposed listing: PulseAI Platform (standard tier) + 3rd-party infra bundle
- Requested credit: one-time 12% listing credit for the first 6 months after publish
- Rationale: enables 3 early enterprise pilots (committed MRR), accelerates co-sell handoffs, and increases listing visibility in marketplace catalogs

I've attached the SOW and the pricing sheet showing committed customers and expected ARR if the pilot converts. We can provide PO/DocuSign once we have sign-off.

Can you escalate to Redwood's deal desk / marketplace team and let us know what documentation you need? We're trying to finalize terms with AWS Marketplace and would appreciate alignment by next week.

Appreciate it —

Neha — thanks for flagging. Quick take from finance/deal desk perspective: 

- Standard policy: deal desk can approve up to 10% one-time listing credit for bundled offers without executive sign-off.
- Anything >10% requires marketplace ops and finance sign-off due to revenue recognition and partner co-sell rules (multi-region adds complexity).

What I need from you / PulseAI ASAP:
- Confirmed committed ARR (by customer) and PO timing (DocuSign or signed PO)
- Clarify whether the credit is purely on Redwood listing fees or applied to total subscription (affects rev share)
- Proposed guardrails: if we approve 12%, ask for a 9-month minimum commitment and milestone-based payout (e.g., 50% on publish, 50% after first invoice).

I'll coordinate with finance and loop in marketplace ops (Marissa) to confirm whether AWS/Azure will accept a 12% one-time waiver for a cross-region bundle. If Marissa confirms marketplace okay, I can route a formal approval request to our SVP of Revenue for the delta.

Ben Carter
